*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City
Council Meeting of May 25, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at
  aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and
  in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence
  should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to
  the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting.
  Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5
  minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from
  landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Social Media or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it
  is requested that you mute the sound of your video feed as it is delayed from the phone transmission.
  Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone line, you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.
  l  Dial-In: 1-888-251-2949 or 1-215-861-0694 using the specific access codes detailed
  below for the respective City Council Dates:
  ¡ May 4, 2021 – Access Code: 2012120# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 11, 2021 – Access Code: 2175831# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 18, 2021 – Access Code: 1813035# wait two seconds and press # again
  ¡ May 25, 2021 – Access Code: 2489941# wait two seconds and press # again

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting;
however, members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access
options 1 and 2 noted above.

Inglewood, California
  May 25, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  May 25, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing
  Authority Member Dotson.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas, other than the public hearing.
  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on the Warrants and Bills.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills, and Agenda Item Nos. 2,
  approval of the Minutes of the Meeting held on November 10, 2020, DR-1, Fiscal Year
  2020-2021 Midyear Budget Review Report, and 6, adoption of a resolution adopting a
  list of projects for Fiscal Year 2021-2022 funded by the Road Repair and Accountability
  Act of 2017. She also spoke regarding Brown Act Violations, specifically about the time
  permitted to speak on Agenda Items.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated May
  21, 2021, in the amount of $2,795,343.23 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member
  Dotson.

178  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – INGLEWOOD TOW SERVICE, INC.;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-91 ADOPTED – TOW REFERRAL PERMIT GRANTED
  TO INGLEWOOD TOW SERVICE, INC. The City Clerk announced the next
  schedule matter was public hearing to receive public comments on the issuance of a tow
  referral permit to Inglewood Tow Service, Inc. to provide City referral towing services,

  1
   May 25, 2021

  notice had been given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was
  on file, and no communications were received.

  Captain DiBernardo, Inglewood Police Department, presented the staff report dated May
  25, 2021.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke in favor of the City receiving 7% but questioned the
  number of tow truck companies that the City needs.

  Gil Mathieu, inquired about B & H Towing, (a towing company that the City used
  previously). He commented in favor of a new contract with Inglewood Tow Service, but
  questioned where the cars would be stored.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-91 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING THE ISSUANCE OF
  CITY REFERRAL TOWING SERVICE PERMITS PURSUANT TO
  CHAPTER 8, ARTICLE 6 OF THE MUNICIPAL CODE

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on November 10, 2020,
  be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None;
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letter from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claim filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1. Seville Hilton for alleged property damage; tree trimming on March 6, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby Reject Claim listed as A-1. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

126  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGISTAR
  RECORDER’S OFFICE.  Staff report dated May 25, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval to pay an invoice submitted by the Los Angeles County
  Registrar-Recorder’s Office for the General Municipal Election held on November 3,
  2020.
.
  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of $427,579.32. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

  2
   May 25, 2021

178  RESOLUTION NO. 21-92 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2020-2021 FISCAL
  YEAR BUDGET TO ADD AN OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  PROGRAM COORDINATOR. Staff report dated May 25, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution amending the 2020-2021 Fiscal Year budget to
  add a Program Coordinator to the Office of Emergency Services.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-92 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-2021 FISCAL YEAR BUDGETED
  POSITIONS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 21-93 ADOPTED - ADOPTION OF A LIST OF PROJECTS
  FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021 – 2022; INCLUSION OF RMRA FUNDS IN THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 BUDGET AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated May 25,
  2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution adopting a list of projects
  for Fiscal Year 2021-2022 that will be funded by the Road Repair and Accountability Act
  of 2017 (SB 1).

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 21-93 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A LIST OF PROJECTS FOR  FISCAL
  YEAR 2021-22 FUNDED BY SB 1: THE ROAD REPAIR AND
  ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 2017

  and; 2) Authorize the inclusion of said fund into the Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Budget to be
  appropriated for the Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) Local
  Streets Resurfacing projects. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

183  RESOLUTION NO. 21-94 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2020 – 2021 ANNUAL
  BUDGET FOR ONGOING CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS. Staff report
  dated May 25, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution amending the
  2020-2021 Annual Budget to provide funding for scheduling changes and change orders
  for various ongoing Capital Improvement Projects.

  It was moved by Council Member Padilla, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby adopt Resolution No. 21-94 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  AMENDING THE 2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO PROVIDE FUNDING
  FOR SCHEDULING CHANGES AND CHANGE ORDERS FOR VARIOUS
  ON-GOING CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Member Dotson.

142  FISCAL YEAR 2020 – 2021 2ND QUARTER/MIDYEAR BUDGET REVIEW
  REPORT RECEIVED AND FILED. Staff report dated May 25, 2021, was presented
  presenting the Fiscal Year 2020 - 2021 Midyear Budget Review Report.

  3
 May 25, 2021

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Budget Manager, presented the 2nd Quarter/Midyear Budget
  Report for Fiscal Year 2020 – 2021.

  Mayor Butts order the 2nd Quarter/Midyear Budget Report for Fiscal Year 2020-2021
  received and filed.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson reported on the City
  Clerk Summit she attended with the Los Angeles County Registrar Recorder’s Office.
  She also stated she received imperative information regarding updates on the upcoming
  election, the expanded partnership initiatives for Vote Centers, Ballot Drop Boxes, and
  updates on election procedures and candidate filing. Additionally, she thanked the Mayor
  and Officer Dixie for assisting her with an issue she experienced. Finally, she asked the
  Mayor to close the meeting in honor of Arlene Darshay Parks, sister of Deputy City Clerk
  Angela Allen.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 6, adoption of a resolution
  adopting a list of projects for Fiscal Year 2021-2022 funded by the Road Repair and
  Accountability Act of 2017, and, 7, amending the 2020-2021 Annual Budget for various
  ongoing Capital Improvement Projects. She also spoke on continuous Brown Act
  Violations, specifically the time limits allowed to speak on Agenda Items. Lastly, she
  requested a response to phone calls and emails.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Item No. DR-1, the Fiscal Year 2020-
  2021 Midyear Budget Review Report.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item No. DR-1, the Fiscal Year 2020-
  2021 Midyear Budget Review Report.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Arlene “Darshay” Parks, sister of Deputy City Clerk Angela
  Allen, at the hour of 2:48 p.m.

  Approved this 21st day of September, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
